family_reason: Separate safety and helpfulness critic LLM roles converse with the coder; tools only ground the critics.
scope_reason: Proposes a critic framework to make generated code safer; evaluated with CyberSecEval insecure-code detector.
gain_metric: Safety: % outputs not flagged by CyberSecEval insecure code detector (CyberSecEval-1 validation split)
gain_quote: Direct Gen 78.2 50.0 64.1 additional instructions are given to models to proINDICT 90.9 81.4 86.1
gain_note: Strongest baseline in the same table is Reflexion+ at 86.9 safety (GPT-4o-mini); 20% validation split of CyberSecEval-1. Extraction headline CommandR 68.2->81.0 is from the helpfulness table (Table 11), not safety.
core_idea: Two LLM critics, one for safety and one for helpfulness, hold an internal dialogue grounded by web search and code execution, giving preemptive and post-hoc feedback to the coder.

family_reason: RL fine-tuning (PPO/GRPO) with correctness-gated speedup reward is the contribution.
scope_reason: Trains an LLM to generate faster assembly; speedup measured by execution.
gain_quote: We evaluate 23 LLMs on this benchmark and find that the strongest baseline, Claude-opus-4, achieves a 51.5% test-passing rate and a 1.43× average speedup over gcc -O3. To further enhance performance, we fine-tune models with reinforcement learning, optimizing a reward function that integrates correctness and performance speedup. Starting from Qwen2.5Coder-7B-Instruct (61.4% correctness, 1.10× speedup), the fine-tuned model SuperCoder attains 95.0% correctness and 1.46× average speedup
gain_note: Speedup is relative to gcc -O3, not 1.0 baseline; base model Qwen2.5-Coder-7B is 1.10x. Assembly-to-assembly optimization of compiler output.
core_idea: Fine-tunes a code LLM with PPO/GRPO using a reward that pays measured speedup over gcc -O3 only when the rewritten assembly passes tests.

family_reason: Performance-conditioned fine-tuning and self-play synthetic data on PIE are the main contribution.
scope_reason: Adapts LLMs to produce faster program edits; speedup measured in gem5 simulation.
baseline_name: GPT-4 with dynamic retrieval prompting, Best@8
gain_quote: Retrieval (O) Retrieval (P) CODELLAMA 34B GPT-4 42.54% 76.07% 2.43× 3.93× 73.62% 95.71% FineTune (O) FineTune (P) CODELLAMA 13B, Perf-Cond GPT-3.5, Self-Play 66.56% 87.63% 5.65× 6.86×
gain_note: Best of 8 generations; baseline and technique use different base models (GPT-4 prompting vs fine-tuned GPT-3.5). Edits human-written slow programs.
core_idea: Fine-tunes code LLMs on a curated dataset of slow-to-fast program edit pairs, adding performance-tag conditioning and self-play synthetic pairs.

family_reason: Learned vulnerability detector filters generated completions; keep v0 (external verifier, not an LLM role).
scope_reason: Filters which LLM completions are shown rather than changing code; most of paper is detector accuracy.
gain_metric: Vulnerability reduction rate (share of scenarios with a CodeQL-flagged completion)
gain_quote: Vulnerability Reduction Rate 71.00% 74.00% 61.96% 89.74%
gain_note: Relative figure: 89.74% reduction for text-davinci-003 (21 of 27 = 78.00% vulnerable scenarios -> 2 of 24 = 8.0%); valid scenario count also drops after filtering. Technique value = 100 - 89.74.
core_idea: A fine-tuned CodeBERT vulnerability classifier screens LLM completions at edit time and suppresses those predicted vulnerable.

family_reason: Main novelty: GNN-predicted parallel pattern inserted into the prompt before generation; no feedback loop.
scope_reason: GNN-guided prompts for OpenMP parallelization; runtime speedup measured.
gain_metric: Average speedup (%) of parallelized code over sequential
baseline_name: GPT-4 with few-shot CoT prompt (no GNN context)
gain_quote: Average speedup(%) gain of GPT-4 is improved by 17.7% (Intel) & 17.2% (AMD) on NAS and by 16.1% (Intel) & 19.5% (AMD)
gain_note: Relative improvement of speedup% read from a figure caption; whether 17.7% is absolute or relative is ambiguous. Incorrect clauses replaced by sequential code in runtime runs.
core_idea: A graph neural network classifies loop parallelism patterns from the program flow graph, and the predicted pattern is injected into the LLM prompt to generate OpenMP pragmas.

family_reason: Prefix-tuning with masked, contrastive and KL losses on curated vulnerability-fix data.
scope_reason: Hardens code LMs to generate secure code; CodeQL security rate on generated programs.
gain_metric: Security rate (% secure among valid programs, CodeQL)
gain_quote: SVENsec increases the security rate from 59.1% to 92.3%.
gain_note: Best-performing model size (2.7B), temperature 0.4; text-prompt and text-ft baselines are reported in ablations.
core_idea: Learns small property-specific continuous prefixes via masked-LM, contrastive and KL losses on security-fix diffs, steering generation toward secure code without changing LM weights.

family_reason: Structured prompt adding functional requirements, domain generalization and domain constraints.
scope_reason: Case study mainly about completeness; readability claim and its instrument unverified (abstract only).
gain_note: Abstract gives only the technique value (comment rate 26.3%) with no baseline comment rate; abstract only, no full text.
core_idea: A prompt template combining functional requirements, generalized domain features and domain constraints for safety-critical code generation.

family_reason: Adds scenario-specific security warnings to the Copilot prompt; pre-generation, no feedback.
scope_reason: Prompt modification to reduce insecure Copilot output; security judged manually.
gain_note: Very small sample (25 per method); the 16% is a percentage-point drop (28%->12%) from a garbled table.
core_idea: Prepends a scenario-specific security warning to the code-completion prompt so Copilot avoids known insecure patterns.

family_reason: Fine-tunes GPT-J on real-world vulnerability-fix data.
scope_reason: Fine-tuning to increase share of non-vulnerable generated C/C++ code.
gain_quote: Our experiments on GPT-J show that the fine-tuned GPT-J achieved 70.4% and 64.5% ratios of non-vulnerable code generation for C and C++, respectively, which has a 10% increase for C and a slight increase for C++ compared with the pre-trained large language model.
gain_note: Abstract only (quote from abstract). "10% increase" may be absolute or relative; technique absolute value is 70.4%.
core_idea: Fine-tunes a code LLM on real-world vulnerability-fixing commits so it learns to produce the patched, secure form of code.

family_reason: Constrained beam sampling with keyword/template constraints during decoding.
scope_reason: Decoding method to raise secure-and-correct generation; CodeQL/Sonar evaluated.
baseline_name: SVEN prefix tuning with unconstrained decoding (CodeGen-2.7B)
gain_quote: Our results show that constrained decoding over CodeGen (51.25% securepass@1) works better than prefix tuning with unconstrained decoding (36.3% secure-pass@1 for SVEN).
gain_note: Constraints written manually per prompt; same-model beam sampling baseline is 33.77, nucleus 26.07.
core_idea: Beam sampling over code LLMs with manually specified positive and negative keyword/template constraints per prompt, enforcing secure API patterns during decoding.

family_reason: Two-phase plan-then-implement few-shot prompting.
scope_reason: Targets correctness; readability only a secondary human rating without numbers.
gain_note: Readability shown only as a violin plot; no numeric baseline/technique pair in text.
core_idea: The LLM first writes a concise step plan from few-shot examples, then generates code conditioned on that plan.

family_reason: Core novelty is a RAG library of HLS repair templates guiding the LLM; compiler loop is secondary.
scope_reason: Repairs human C into HLS-C; efficiency is hardware PPA of synthesized circuits.
gain_quote: an average reduction of 36.57%, 33.03%, and 29.08% in area, power, and minimum clock period, respectively.
gain_note: Relative reduction on 5 benchmarks read from figure; baseline is unoptimized design, not another LLM method. Technique = 100 - 36.57.
core_idea: Retrieves HLS repair templates and iterates LLM repair with compiler feedback, then has the LLM write bit-width and pragma optimization scripts to reduce PPA.

family_reason: Evolutionary loop driven by execution-based selection of representative samples; retrieval is an auxiliary component.
scope_reason: Search-based LLM optimization of programs; speedup measured by execution.
gain_metric: SP@5 speedup rate (%) on Python, GPT-4
gain_note: Columns are Instruction, ICL, RAG, COT, SBLLM; GPT-4 on 10% test sample; top-5 selection. Edits human-written slow programs (PIE).
core_idea: Iteratively evolves candidate optimizations by selecting representative executed samples, retrieving optimization patterns and applying genetic-operator-style CoT prompts to combine them.

family_reason: Oracle-guided synthetic secure data plus LoRA fine-tuning is the main contribution.
scope_reason: Fine-tunes code LLMs to generate fewer CodeQL-flagged vulnerabilities.
gain_metric: Number of vulnerable codes among top-5 samples (CodeQL, CodeLMSec)
gain_quote: Figure 6a shows that using our HexaCoder, the model generates 65 vulnerable codes among the top-5 sampled codes, while SVEN [35] and the pre-trained CodeGen-2B-multi [52] generate 368 and 456 vulnerable codes, respectively.
gain_note: Count of vulnerable samples, not a rate; pre-trained model 456.
core_idea: Uses CodeQL as an oracle to have GPT-4 repair vulnerable samples into secure synthetic training pairs, then LoRA-fine-tunes code LLMs and generates with a two-step library-first procedure.

family_reason: Generated code is checked by an AST detector against an outdated-API database and regenerated with a ban list.
scope_reason: Reduces outdated/vulnerable API use in generated Python code.
gain_quote: APILOT can reduce outdated code recommendations by 89.42% on average with limited performance overhead.
gain_note: Relative reduction averaged over 7 LLMs; custom detector and self-built benchmark. Technique = 100 - 89.42.
core_idea: Sanitizes generated code by AST-matching APIs against a curated outdated-API database, then regenerates with a ban list of the flagged APIs.

family_reason: Static analyzer messages are turned into repair prompts fed back to the model.
scope_reason: Repairs code-smell and security-smell issues in generated code using analyzer feedback.
gain_metric: % prompts with at least one smell-free suggestion after repair
baseline_name: Pre-repair top-1 suggestion with quality issues
gain_note: Only "up to 80%" of prompts repaired; no pre-repair comparison value given (repair prompts start from flawed suggestions). Mixes security and code smells.
core_idea: Builds a repair prompt from the static analyzer message (generated-knowledge prompting, three structures) and re-queries the LLM to fix quality issues.

family_reason: Efficiency-aware supervised fine-tuning on curated efficient solutions.
scope_reason: Fine-tunes LLMs to generate faster code; execution time measured.
gain_metric: Average execution time of correct code (EffiBench)
gain_quote: decreases from 0.31 (s) to 0.16 (s), a reduction of 48.4%.
gain_note: Computed on tasks correct for both models; PIE/Mercury fine-tuning baselines also reported.
core_idea: Builds an instruction dataset of solutions iteratively optimized for runtime by LLMs with execution profiling, then fine-tunes code LLMs on it.

family_reason: Fine-tunes DeepSeek Coder on company code data.
scope_reason: Abstract only; unclear whether maintainability/efficiency are measured on the code; likely thesis.
gain_note: Abstract only; no numbers reported.
core_idea: Fine-tunes a 6.7B code model on proprietary business code to generate patches that meet evolving requirements.

family_reason: Execution feedback from the most time-consuming unit test drives refinement.
scope_reason: Execution-feedback refinement to improve runtime of generated code.
gain_note: Printed delta (+13.14) does not match difference (13.04); vs base model, not strongest refinement baseline; tests used as both feedback and evaluation.
core_idea: After correctness refinement, executes candidate code on unit tests, reports the slowest test and its time, and asks the LLM to optimize accordingly.

family_reason: Several specialized LLM agents (planner, detector, predator, ranker, handler) collaborate.
scope_reason: Exception-handling robustness; quality via unnamed review score and LLM judge.
gain_note: Table columns: General Prompting, Traditional RAG, KPC, FuzzyCatch, Nexgen, Seeker; underlying model for Table 1 unclear; tool behind ACRS unnamed.
core_idea: Agents scan fragile code, retrieve exception knowledge from a common-exception enumeration via deep RAG, rank exception types and generate try-catch handling.

family_reason: GNN semantic/vulnerability analysis feeds back into regeneration.
scope_reason: Abstract only, low-profile venue; unclear whether security score measures generated code.
gain_note: Abstract only; no numbers reported.
core_idea: A fine-tuned transformer generates code, a GNN over ASTs and semantic graphs detects logic errors and vulnerabilities, and flagged code is regenerated.

family_reason: RL with rewards from program-analysis detectors and unit tests.
scope_reason: RL training for secure and maintainable generated code; detector-based evaluation.
gain_note: Evaluation detectors are the same as the training reward (bias in favour of REAL); vanilla is 0.3902.
core_idea: GRPO-style RL whose reward combines vulnerability/maintainability findings from automated program analysis with unit-test functionality, needing no human labels.

family_reason: Novelty is contextual retrieval of optimization examples guiding the search.
scope_reason: LLM program optimization for speed; gem5-measured speedup.
gain_quote: On PIE, RAS significantly outperforms dynamic retrieval, a state-of-the-art blackbox adaptation strategy, achieving an 8.70× average speedup compared to 4.23× for dynamic retrieval using Qwen3Coder.
gain_note: Edits human-written slow programs; LLM calls normalized across baselines; best-of-search speedup.
core_idea: The LLM writes natural-language descriptions of programs to retrieve relevant slow-fast examples and uses them in an iterative search over candidate optimizations.

family_reason: LLM-aware selection of in-context examples to retrieve.
scope_reason: Targets correctness via example selection; quality only via human rating not targeted.
gain_metric: Human code-quality rating (0-2, absence of bad smells)
gain_quote: Particularly, our LAIL surpasses the SOTA approach by 5.811% in code quality and 7.027% in maintainability.
gain_note: Relative improvement of a human rating (LAIL 1.839 vs 1.738); no agreement statistic; model for human evaluation unspecified.
core_idea: Labels candidate examples by how much they raise the LLM's own likelihood of the correct answer, trains a contrastive retriever on these labels and selects in-context examples with it.

family_reason: Adds CFG and data-mapping table to the prompt; keep v0.
scope_reason: Decompilation; readability metric is edit similarity to original source (fidelity).
gain_metric: Normalized edit similarity (ES) to original source
baseline_name: Same LLMs prompted with raw assembly
gain_note: Decompilation fidelity only; reported as absolute improvement (8.36% on HumanEval-Decompile) averaged over three models.
core_idea: Augments decompilation prompts with a control-flow graph and a data-mapping table derived from the binary.

family_reason: Structured decomposition into data-flow diagrams drives generation; human interaction not a tool signal.
scope_reason: Builds data-analysis systems; code quality reported but not the stated target; two case studies.
baseline_name: Low Code baseline (best of LLM-k / CP-k)
gain_quote: For PHY, iProg achieves logic scores of 6.69/10 compared to 1.71–1.88 for Low Code baselines.
gain_note: Single case study, single engineer; iProg code is much longer (259 vs 48-50 lines); 1.88 is the top of a range.
core_idea: Decomposes the task into a data-flow diagram and generates each module through a two-way intelligibility protocol between engineer and LLM.

family_reason: Searches over multi-agent workflow graphs (MCTS) for Verilog generation; keep v0.
scope_reason: Verilog workflow mainly for correctness; area/power of synthesized hardware secondary.
gain_note: Single module of 9; columns Designer, IO, PromptV, AFlow, VFlow (area/power/slack); timing slack worse than IO. Hardware PPA.
core_idea: Cooperative-evolution Monte Carlo tree search over multiple populations of agentic workflows, scoring workflows with compiler, test and synthesis feedback.

family_reason: Retrieves and injects security knowledge into RACG prompts; keep v0.
scope_reason: Security knowledge injection for retrieval-augmented code generation; CyberSecEval detector.
gain_metric: Security rate (CyberSecEval ICD), averaged across LLMs
gain_note: Average over six LLMs in the clean RACG setting; 20.12% is relative.
core_idea: Builds a security knowledge base from vulnerability data, decomposes queries into sub-tasks, re-ranks and filters knowledge by CWE prevalence, and injects it into the generation prompt.

family_reason: Iterative energy-profiling feedback with self-correction is the core loop.
scope_reason: LLM refactoring of parallel codes to cut GPU energy; measured energy.
gain_note: Expected energy reduction at k=1 across devices; headline 36%/34% averages are conditional on passing trials; correctness screened by LLM judge.
core_idea: Builds context and a plan, then iteratively refactors code using measured GPU energy, compile/run feedback and self-correction, with an LLM judge screening validity.

family_reason: LLM edits HLS code with synthesis feedback for issue resolution and pragma insertion; keep v0.
scope_reason: Hardware latency of LLM-edited HLS code for ML accelerators; abstract only.
gain_quote: Our LHS allows us to achieve up to 2690 × latency improvement.
gain_note: Abstract only (quote from abstract); "up to" maximum vs unoptimized design; beats hls4ml in only 4 of 6 cases with area overhead.
core_idea: Uses LLMs to resolve HLS synthesis issues, modify source code and insert optimization pragmas for CNN accelerator designs.

family_reason: Beam search over plans/implementations with hardware correctness and performance feedback.
scope_reason: LLM optimization of accelerator kernels; measured latency.
gain_quote: On Gemmini, Autocomp speeds up GEMMs by 5.6× compared to the vendor-provided library and 1.4× compared to expert-level hand-tuned code
gain_note: No plain-LLM baseline in headline; starts from unoptimized code; 5.6x is vs vendor library.
core_idea: Two-phase plan-then-implement prompting with an optimization menu, menu dropout and LLM ensembling inside a beam search scored by hardware latency.

family_reason: Synthesized performance-stressing tests supply execution-profile feedback to the optimizer.
scope_reason: Better performance feedback improves LLM code optimization; CPU instruction counts measured.
gain_note: Values are % improvements over the original slow programs (None / CC default / PerfForge); optimizes human-written solutions; correctness of optimized code not reported.
core_idea: Uses an LLM to synthesize performance-characterizing constraints and constraint-aware fuzzing to create stressing inputs, whose execution profiles feed the code optimizer.

family_reason: GRPO with a static-analysis quality reward added to correctness reward.
scope_reason: RL to improve analyzer-measured quality of generated code.
gain_note: Single aggregate score mixing maintainability, security and efficiency findings; synthetic code-editing tasks.
core_idea: Adds a reward from a severity-weighted static code-quality analyzer to correctness and format rewards during GRPO training.

family_reason: Main novelty is the UI grouping chain and hierarchy-aware divide-and-conquer prompting; refinement is secondary.
scope_reason: UI code generation aiming at structured, maintainable code; human ratings.
gain_quote: readability (4.75 vs. 4.43), and maintainability (4.32 vs. 3.32).
gain_note: Small user study (5 developers), no agreement statistic; readability gain is 4.43->4.75.
core_idea: Groups UI elements into a component hierarchy with a multimodal chain, generates code per subtree, then self-corrects using rendered-screenshot comparison.

family_reason: Retrieves OpenMP tutorial passages into the prompt; keep v0.
scope_reason: Main claim is compilable OpenMP; runtime not compared against a baseline.
gain_note: Runtime measured only for P4OMP outputs as speedup over the same code at 1 thread (7.82 s -> 1.36 s for Jacobi 2D); no baseline efficiency comparison.
core_idea: Retrieval-augmented prompting with an OpenMP tutorial corpus to guide an LLM in inserting parallel pragmas into serial C++ code.

family_reason: Function-oriented instruction tuning plus style-oriented list-wise contrastive learning.
scope_reason: Code translation; style measured as similarity to reference translation, a readability proxy.
gain_metric: CSSim style similarity to reference translation
gain_note: Garbled Table 4; column mapping (GPT-4 Direct/CoT/RAG/Self-debug, then F2STrans Qwen0.5B-7B, StarCoder3B) inferred; similarity-to-reference metric.
core_idea: Fine-tunes translation LLMs first on functionally correct translations, then with list-wise contrastive learning that ranks candidates by style similarity to the source.

family_reason: Agent loop with execution/profiling feedback, Reflexion debugging and LLM optimizer drives results.
scope_reason: Agentic generation of Triton GPU kernels; measured speedup.
gain_metric: Average speedup over reference kernels (TritonBench-revised, MI300)
gain_quote: On MI300, GEAK achieves 54.89% execution accuracy and a 2.59× speedup on TritonBench-revised Benchmark, and 63.33% execution accuracy and 0.92x speedup on ROCm Benchmark
gain_note: Speedup over reference kernels, computed only over correct kernels; direct-prompting speedups are over different correct subsets; 0.92x on ROCm benchmark.
core_idea: An agent combining knowledge injection, one-shot retrieval, Reflexion-style debugging, an LLM optimizer using latency feedback and parallel scaling to produce Triton kernels.

family_reason: Evolutionary loop: SLM mutations selected by compiler, test and profiler fitness.
scope_reason: Legacy-system evolution with thin methodology; code quality outcomes not clearly attributable.
gain_quote: Experiments show a 40% latency reduction and a sevenfold drop in feature lead time compared with strong baselines.
gain_note: Relative reduction; baseline not identified; Table 1 garbled; also claims 83% of known vulnerabilities fixed (no baseline pair). Credibility should be checked.
core_idea: Represents code, builds, docs and tickets as a typed graph and evolves them with small-model mutation operators selected by multi-objective Pareto and novelty fitness under a safety gate.

family_reason: Novelty is the SmartFSM intermediate representation guiding generation; fine-tuning and feedback are add-ons.
scope_reason: FSM-guided smart contract generation to reduce Slither-detected vulnerabilities.
gain_metric: Vulnerability risk score VRS (Slither severity x confidence)
gain_note: VRS set to 10 for non-compiling code, so compilation gains inflate security; Direct baseline 7.4416; FSM-SCG includes fine-tuning and feedback.
core_idea: Converts requirements into a finite-state-machine representation (SmartFSM) that guides contract code generation, plus fine-tuning and compile/security feedback refinement.

family_reason: Bandit/Pylint findings fed back iteratively for revision; keep v0.
scope_reason: Static-analysis feedback loop improves security and readability of GPT-4o code.
baseline_name: Initial GPT-4o generation (no refinement), All-issues configuration
gain_note: Columns are Insecure(Initial) then Insecure(After) for Select 1,2,3,5,All; baseline is pre-refinement code only; up to ten iterations.
core_idea: Iteratively selects a subset of Bandit and Pylint issues by severity and frequency and prompts the LLM to fix them, repeating for up to ten rounds.

family_reason: SonarLint warnings given to the LLM for refactoring; keep v0.
scope_reason: Mostly an empirical comparison of LLM readability; refactoring prompt is not a new technique.
gain_note: Only between-LLM comparison (DeepSeek 83% vs ChatGPT 76% vs Gemini 62% corrected); no technique-vs-baseline pair; behaviour preservation not checked.
core_idea: Prompts an LLM with SonarLint readability warnings for its own snippet and asks it to refactor them.

family_reason: Profiler-guided evolutionary search with planner LLM; execution profiles are the key signal.
scope_reason: LLM optimization of GPU rendering kernels; measured execution time.
gain_metric: Average performance improvement over original kernels
gain_quote: feeding additional information from performance profilers, the performance improvement increases to 42% and 38% on average with Deepseek.
gain_note: Relative improvement over original code (best-effort manual version reaches 39%); falls from 68% during search; figures only; manual bug fixes for some kernels.
core_idea: A planner LLM uses profiler data to prune the optimization search space, then evolutionary search (OpenEvolve) mutates kernels with an LLM cross-check for equivalence.

family_reason: Trust-weighted federated fine-tuning with human security feedback.
scope_reason: Questionable paper: unnamed SAST, implausible closed-model FL, simulation only.
gain_metric: Vulnerability generation rate (VGR) on hold-out set
gain_quote: After 100 rounds, the VGR dropped from an initial 7.4% to 4.1%.
gain_note: Simulated results; instrument unclear; credibility should be verified.
core_idea: Federated fine-tuning where client updates are weighted by a trust metric to resist poisoning while incorporating developer security feedback.

family_reason: Same LLM reasons over a secure-coding-practice graph to refine its own seed solution.
scope_reason: Graph-guided reasoning to make generated code secure; CodeQL security rate.
gain_note: Columns Zero-Shot, PaS, PromSec, GRASP (Table 3, GPT-4o); vs base model the GPT-4o rate rises 0.61->0.82.
core_idea: Organizes secure coding practices into a dependency graph and has the LLM traverse relevant practices to revise its seed code.

family_reason: Pre-generation performance-aware prompt built from bottleneck diagnosis and retrieved directives.
scope_reason: Prompting to raise speed of optimized code; gem5-measured speedup.
gain_quote: on GPT-o4-mini, standard prompting yields only a 1.99× speedup, whereas ECO raises to 7.81×—nearly a four-fold gain.
gain_note: Best of 5; vs instruction-only rather than SBLLM/RAG baselines; fine-tuning beats ECO on 7B.
core_idea: A symbolic advisor diagnoses performance bottlenecks with static analysis and an ROI retriever fetches matching optimization directives, combined into a performance-aware prompt.

family_reason: Retrieves optimization strategies from a library, located via LLM-generated Semgrep rules; keep v0.
scope_reason: LLM code optimization guided by strategies; performance and patch-match evaluated.
gain_metric: Semantic equivalence to developer optimization patch (SemEqv), C/C++, DeepSeek-V3
gain_note: Metric is match to developer optimization patches, not measured speedup; measured in-the-wild speedups (5.04%-218.07%) have no baseline. Edits human-written code.
core_idea: Builds a library of optimization strategies from historical commits, has the LLM write Semgrep rules to locate applicable code, and prompts the LLM to apply the matched strategy.

family_reason: RAG over a decompilation-distortion database guides detection and correction; keep v0.
scope_reason: Corrects decompiler output fidelity; not LLM-generated or edited source-quality target.
gain_metric: Fix Rate (FR) of decompilation distortions, manual
gain_quote: model, DeGPT, which achieved an average Fix Rate (FR) of 83% and an average Corrected Fix Rate (CFR) of 37%, FidelityGPT demonstrated superior performance. With an average FR of 94%
gain_note: Decompilation fidelity; FR is a manual fix rate rather than a readability metric.
core_idea: Retrieves similar distortion patterns from a database by semantic intensity and uses variable-dependency analysis to prompt the LLM to detect and correct decompilation distortions.

family_reason: Planner, programmer, reviewer and evaluator LLM roles collaborate, with synthesis reports in context.
scope_reason: Verilog RTL; efficiency is hardware PPA of synthesized designs.
baseline_name: Baseline LLM-generated RTL (VeriOpt before PPA optimization)
gain_quote: Experimental results demonstrate up to 88% reduction in power, 76% reduction in area and 73% improvement in timing closure compared to baseline LLM-generated RTL
gain_note: "Up to" maximum over designs; per-design results mixed; baseline is the method's own pre-optimization code; single model and run.
core_idea: Assigns planner, programmer, reviewer and evaluator roles to GPT-4o and feeds synthesis PPA reports back as in-context examples to optimize RTL.

family_reason: EDA tool logs turned into iterative improvement prompts; keep v0.
scope_reason: Mainly a benchmark; Log2BetterRTL is an add-on for RTL (hardware) code.
gain_note: Abstract only; only deltas reported ("reduces lint violations by up to 229", clarity +0.51), no baseline/technique values.
core_idea: Converts EDA tool diagnostics (lint, synthesis logs) into iterative improvement prompts for RTL code.

family_reason: Security-centric rewriting of risky prompts before generation; keep v0.
scope_reason: Abstract reports prompt rectification counts, not measured security of generated code.
gain_note: Abstract only; 471 of 509 risky prompts rectified is a detection count, not a code-security gain vs baseline.
core_idea: Detects prompts likely to lead to insecure code and rewrites their potentially insecure descriptions to steer the code generator.

family_reason: Multi-objective DPO with blockchain-specific metrics.
scope_reason: Preference optimization for gas-efficient and secure smart contracts.
gain_note: Abstract only; gives technique values (58.9% Gas@5, 62.5% Secure@5) but no baseline values.
core_idea: Extends DPO to rank contract samples by quantified gas cost, security and correctness metrics jointly for multi-objective alignment.

family_reason: Requirement, generation, verification and optimization agents collaborate; RAG and LoRA support them.
scope_reason: Multi-agent PLC code generation with maintainability measured in a case study.
gain_note: Single case study; MI tool not named; model inside the system unspecified; manual code scores 88.
core_idea: Splits PLC code generation across requirement-analysis, generation, verification and optimization agents with retrieval, hierarchical prompting and LoRA domain adaptation.

family_reason: Outdated-API dataset used for cache prediction and augmented generation; keep v0.
scope_reason: Reduces outdated/vulnerable API recommendations in generated code.
gain_quote: The results demonstrate that APILOT reduces outdated API recommendations by an average of 75%, with some models achieving up to 100% mitigation in specific large language models.
gain_note: Abstract only (quote from abstract); relative reduction averaged over 17 LLMs; journal version of R01272.
core_idea: Maintains a quickly updatable dataset of outdated APIs and uses cache prediction and augmented generation to steer LLMs away from them.

family_reason: Iterative LLM-driven verification and repair of Verilog by the same model.
scope_reason: Repair loop is correctness-focused; efficiency compared against HLS, not against LLM without technique.
gain_note: Abstract only; no numbers for resources or frequency.
core_idea: Prompts LLMs to generate Verilog, verify it and iteratively repair the defects they characterize.

family_reason: Model self-checks and reflects using a prompt engine and reflective memory; core is reflection.
scope_reason: Reflection module to raise security of agent-generated code; CodeQL measured.

family_reason: LLM generation alternates with symbolic-execution verification feedback.

family_reason: Generated code is verified against declared security contracts and blocked or allowed.
scope_reason: Verification pipeline reduces vulnerabilities in AI-generated code.

family_reason: Evolutionary search driven by measured runtime feedback; keep v0.

core_idea: Evolutionary code search with hierarchical context management, momentum-based backtracking and adaptive collaboration among islands for long-horizon progress.

family_reason: Main novelty is a meta-corrected process reward model for best-of-N selection.

core_idea: Prompts the LLM to write code function by function, treating each function as a PRM step, and selects among N samples using a meta-learning-corrected PRM.

family_reason: Distills security knowledge into a 7B model.
scope_reason: Distillation to reduce injection vulnerabilities in generated code.

gain_note: Abstract only (quote from abstract); relative figure; instrument and benchmark unknown.

family_reason: Translator, fixer, judge and optimizer agents with HLS feedback; keep v0.

gain_note: No plain-LLM baseline; best of multiple runs per kernel; resource usage worse than baselines.

family_reason: RL with verifiable correctness and speedup rewards on GPT-5.
scope_reason: RL fine-tuning for faster GPU kernels; measured speedup.

family_reason: Online GRPO with real-machine GFLOPS reward.

family_reason: Main novelty is domain-specific ICL+CoT prompting with optimization rules; repair loop targets correctness.

family_reason: Executable checks derived from instruction files flag violations fed back to the agent in-loop.
scope_reason: Compliance with agent instruction files mixes style, architecture and process rules; oracle is its own checks.

family_reason: Knowledge graph of knowledge, behavior and skills assembled dynamically into prompts; keep v0.
scope_reason: Maintainability gains measured against human legacy code in a single human-in-the-loop refactoring.
gain_note: Single case; baseline is legacy human code, not an LLM baseline; also MI 59 -> 66.
core_idea: A three-track knowledge graph (knowledge, behaviour, skills) is queried to assemble prompts dynamically, with plan-first execution and role separation for agentic WebGIS coding.

family_reason: Activation steering of the residual stream during decoding; keep v0.
scope_reason: Steering to make generated code secure; CodeQL/Sonar and CWEval evaluated.
gain_note: Vs vanilla; hybrid with constrained decoding gives 27.9% relative gain on CWEval (Llama3.1-8B); correctness mixed.
core_idea: Extracts a secure-code concept direction by difference in means of residual activations and adds it to the residual stream at inference to steer generation.

family_reason: Separate summarization, analysis, optimization and evaluation agents collaborate; keep v0.

gain_note: Single system, single model, single run; no LLM baseline; edits human-written code.

family_reason: RAG repair library of reference templates is the key component guiding refactoring.

family_reason: Differential profiling and correctness reflection drive iterative mixture-of-prompts optimization.

family_reason: Fine-tuning on code refined by the SAST feedback framework.

family_reason: Generator-Reviewer-Revisor debate with difficulty-aware decomposition; keep v0.

gain_note: Abstract only; no numbers reported.

family_reason: Mitigation knowledge base retrieved into a chain-of-thought prompt; keep v0.

family_reason: LLM risk analysis elicits relevant security context into the prompt before generation; keep v0.

family_reason: Core is a learned scheduler choosing typed algorithm-design skill prompts; MCTS supports search.

family_reason: Multi-task fine-tuning with efficiency skeleton supervision.

core_idea: Extracts structured efficiency skeletons (algorithmic templates) from efficient solutions and fine-tunes models jointly to generate skeletons and full code.

gain_note: Abstract only (quote from abstract); relative reduction; models, tool and tasks unknown.
core_idea: Uses explainable-AI analysis of static-analysis findings to identify why smells appear, then rewrites prompts to avoid those causes.

family_reason: Energy-contrastive SFT plus GRPO with simulator-in-the-loop energy reward.

family_reason: Multi-source evidence and cross-scenario examples retrieved to guide optimization.

family_reason: Post-edit functional tuning with edit-aware regularization.

gain_note: Relative gain averaged over models; gains at T = 0.1/0.4/0.8.
core_idea: After a security model edit, fine-tunes for functionality with an L2 penalty that keeps the edited weights close, restoring correctness while preserving security.

family_reason: Separate validator LLM produces enriched findings that the generator LLM remediates.

core_idea: Generates kernels through an intermediate structured representation, verifies them by synthesis-based checks and evolves them with feedback-adaptive refinement.

family_reason: Governed security requirements retrieved from a knowledge graph via MCP before generation.

family_reason: Narrative reformulation of the problem in the prompt; keep v0.
